ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule (`NetEndOfMonth` in `Invoicing.dueDate`) and the terms wording (`Documents.termsText`) are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The parse of the form text into `NetEndOfMonth` is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The storage codec is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code is touched, so no domain rule is decided there.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added anywhere. `dueDate` uses only pure `DateOnly` and `DateTime.DaysInMonth` arithmetic. The parsing, codec and text changes are pure. The clock is not read.

evidence.quote: | _ -> Error "Terms are a number of days between 0 and 365, optionally followed by EOM, or empty for the organization's default."
| true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(Net days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The 1..365 range and the full error message are now written twice, once in the EOM branch and once in the plain-days branch. The "Net {days} EOM" wording is also written in both `termsText` and `termsWords`. The existing `Net` case already did this, so the change follows that pattern. All copies agree, so this is restatement, not contradiction.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The next-month due-date rule and the `ordinal` wording helper are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The form parsing is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The stored-day check is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). All of this stays in Tier 1/2, and Tier 3 and Tier 4 are not touched.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added. `dueDate` and `ordinal` are pure, and the parsing and codec changes are pure.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day) else Error "A day of next month is from 1 to 28"
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
| DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The 1..28 day limit is a literal in both the storage decoder and the engine parser. It has no single definition on the `DayOfNextMonth` type. The "Due the {ordinal day} of next month" wording is also written in both `termsText` and `termsWords`. The copies agree, and `ordinal` is defined once and shared. The error message is improved, since it is now a single local `message` binding. The 1..365 range is still repeated. This counts as restatement and not a contradiction, but the limit could drift.
